subject: MAP: staged commit timeline, pricing slate, and renewal uplift
messages:
From: Erin Wells <erin.wells@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Liu <jared.liu@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + initial commit ask

Vanessa / Rishi —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Internally we've sketched a 10-week evaluation plan but there's pressure from procurement to have a clearer path to commit before the end of Q3. Two asks from my side to make that work: a concrete staged-commit cadence tied to MAP milestones, and visibility into any uplift language that would be applied at renewal if we hit or miss those milestones.

Can you: 1) add a proposed milestone schedule (week-by-week) that maps to commits/discount tiers, and 2) outline what a renewal uplift looks like if our production ramp hits 50% vs 100% of the forecast? Jared is copied for procurement questions.

Attachment: "evaluation-track-telemetry.csv" contains our current token estimates by route.

Best,
Erin
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Erin Wells <erin.wells@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + initial commit ask

Erin, Jared —

Thanks for the clear asks. I've attached a first-pass MAP (Acme_MAP-v1.pdf) and a pricing slate that shows staged-commit thresholds and the corresponding discount / capacity guarantee tiers. High-level summary here so it's easy to circulate internally: 

- Week 1-2: Proof-of-concept + telemetry validation (no commit)
- Week 3-4: Pilot (POC -> pilot) — optional 3-month pilot credit; if pilot acceptance criteria met, move to a 3-month committed pool at 20% of forecast (Tier A discount applies)
- Week 5-8: Ramp to 50% committed pool — trigger additional 10% discount and 1-month extended console retention for logs
- Week 9-12: Full ramp to 100% forecast — final committed tier with maximum discount and priority capacity (SLA uplift)

Renewal uplift language (short): if actual consumption at renewal is >= 90% of committed baseline for the prior 12 months, ACME retains Tier pricing; 60-90% results in a staged uplift of unit-pricing that scales linearly up to +15% at 60%; <60% triggers a remediation review and potential rebaseline. If you prefer, we can convert those bands into floor/ceiling $/K-token numbers.

I'm looping in Rishi and Marissa to confirm the discount math and proposed DocuSign flow for staged acceptance.

Attachments: Acme_MAP-v1.pdf, pricing-slate-Q3-2026.xlsx

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Erin Wells <erin.wells@acme.com>, Jared Liu <jared.liu@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + initial commit ask

Quick notes on the numbers — Vanessa, the attached pricing slate assumes a 12-month baseline for committed units. For a staged-commit approach we recommend: 

- Pilot credits to be applied as a one-time offset in month 1; no adjustment to baseline.
- When moving to a 3-month committed pool (20% forecast): we lock unit-price for those 3 months and count usage toward the 12-month baseline.
- If the customer reaches 50% of forecast by month 2 of ramp, auto-trigger the next tranche pricing in month 3 (no retroactive adjustments).

For renewal uplift specifics: propose the following concrete formula so procurement has something numeric to evaluate: 
- If 12mo actual >= 90% baseline: renewal price = current price
- If 70% <= 12mo actual < 90%: renewal price = current price * (1 + (90% - actual) * 0.25)
- If 50% <= 12mo actual < 70%: renewal price = current price * (1 + (90% - actual) * 0.4) + $0.002 baseline 'rebaseline' fee per K tokens
- If actual < 50%: executive review for rebaseline and potential termination of committed terms

I can convert that to per-token numbers against the sheet if you want. Also note: we can soften uplift bands for strategic accounts in first renewal (apply a cap of +8%).

—
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Erin Wells <erin.wells@acme.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + initial commit ask

Erin —

Appreciate the timeline clarity. Two operational items from CS to make the MAP executable: 

1) Telemetry gating: we need the evaluation routes you shared to be instrumented with the x-rt and token tags so we can validate consumption automatically. If you can provide a short list of 5 priority endpoints we will include them in the acceptance criteria.

2) Attachments / handoff: once the pilot acceptance is signed we will provision a dedicated monitoring Slack channel and set up a weekly cadence for the first 8 weeks (2x for initial ramp). Please confirm the primary contacts for the weekly check-ins (name + email).

I will also prepare a 'first renewal' concession that caps any uplift to +8% for the initial 12-month renewal; I'll add that language to the DocuSign if you want it included in the commitment package.

Thanks — if that all looks okay we can generate a DocuSign today and target a signed staged-commit by next Tuesday.

—
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
